data.summary: The five‑week plan front‑loads the weak Unit 3 early, then moves through the remaining units in a logical order, ending with a mixed review and timed practice. Each week balances theory, practice problems, and a live class (week 2) while staying within the 15‑hour limit.

weeks.focus: Build a solid foundation in kinematics and forces.
tasks: Watch the textbook videos for 1.1‑1.3 and take concise notes (2 h).
Do 15 free‑response kinematics problems, checking answers with the scoring guide (3 h).
Create a one‑page cheat sheet of vector addition rules and displacement‑velocity‑acceleration relationships (1 h).
Complete 10 free‑response problems on free‑body diagrams and Newton's First Law (2 h).
Complete a set of 12 multiple‑choice questions covering 2.1‑2.2 (2 h).
Review mistakes, rewrite solutions, and summarize key formulas (2 h).
Spend 3 h on a timed mixed‑practice set (5 kinematics + 5 dynamics) to build stamina.

weeks.focus: Strengthen Work, Energy, and Power – weak unit.
tasks: Read the AP review chapter on Work, Energy, and Power; annotate examples for 3.1‑3.5 (2 h).
Do 12 free‑response questions on Work (3.2) and Conservation of Energy (3.4), grading with the scoring guide (3 h).
Join Live Class 10500, participate in the Q&A, and note any misconceptions (1 h).
Complete 8 practice problems on Translational Kinetic Energy (3.1) and Power (3.5) (2 h).
Create flashcards for the key equations (KE = ½mv², W = F·d, etc.) and review them in short bursts (1 h).
Take a 20‑minute timed mini‑quiz covering all five sub‑topics, then review errors (2 h).
Spend the remaining 4 h revisiting any weak spots from the live class and re‑doing the most missed problems.

weeks.focus: Linear momentum and introduction to rotational dynamics.
tasks: Watch tutorial videos on linear momentum and impulse; summarize the conservation principle (2 h).
Solve 10 free‑response problems on momentum conservation in collisions (3 h).
Do 8 problems linking linear and rotational motion (5.2) – e.g., rolling without slipping (2 h).
Create a comparison table of linear vs. angular quantities (1 h).
Complete a mixed set of 12 multiple‑choice questions covering 4.1‑4.3 and 5.1‑5.2 (2 h).
Review all solutions, write brief explanations for each step (2 h).
Finish the week with a 30‑minute timed practice on momentum and rotational kinematics (3 h).

weeks.focus: Rotational energy, torque work, and simple harmonic motion.
tasks: Read the AP section on rotational kinetic energy and torque work; annotate key formulas (2 h).
Do 10 free‑response questions on rotational kinetic energy (6.1) and torque‑work (6.2) (3 h).
Complete 6 problems on angular impulse and angular momentum conservation (6.3) (2 h).
Watch a video on simple harmonic motion fundamentals; list the defining equations (1 h).
Solve 12 free‑response SHM problems covering 7.1‑7.3 (3 h).
Create a one‑page summary linking energy concepts across linear and rotational systems (1 h).
Take a 25‑minute timed mixed set (rotational + SHM) and review errors (3 h).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed full‑section practice.
tasks: Review flashcards for all vector, force, and energy equations (2 h).
Do a 40‑minute timed practice set covering at least one problem from each unit (5 h).
Mark the practice set against the AP scoring guidelines; note any recurring errors (2 h).
Re‑work the five most missed problems with step‑by‑step solutions (3 h).
Complete a quick‑fire 20‑question multiple‑choice review of fluid concepts (8.1‑8.4) (1 h).
Write a one‑page exam‑day strategy sheet (what to do first, time allocation, stress‑relief tricks) (1 h).
Spend the final hour doing a brief mindfulness/relaxation routine to prepare for the exam.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, focus on solidifying connections between topics, practice under timed conditions, and refine your test‑taking strategy. Trust the work you’ve done, address the few lingering weak spots, and keep a calm, confident mindset for the exam.
